features.name: Maintenance agents (issue fixer + PR reviewer)
features.description: Two autonomous agents that work this repository's own backlog, each an ordinary workflow so every phase is a persisted, inspectable state output rather than a framework black box. The fixer (`issue-fix`) loads a labelled issue, investigates the checkout, plans a minimal fix, edits the tree, verifies with ruff/mypy/pytest, and opens a PR that links the issue; a failed verification, a non-actionable issue, or a guard trip ends the run at the single Blocked terminal. The reviewer (`pr-review`) reads a PR's diff and submits APPROVE or REQUEST_CHANGES - it never merges; a human does. Guardrails are deterministic checks in the task bodies, never prompt instructions: the opt-in label gate (only a human applies it), a guarded-path check (CI, .env), a workspace confined to the root that refuses secret files and non-allowlisted commands (git read-only), and a publisher that can only push the agent's own branch. Every side effect sits behind a seam (GitHubClient/Workspace/Coder/Reviewer/RepoPublisher) so the shipped state machine runs hermetically with the model, network, token, and checkout all faked. Reviewed/monitored at /admin and in Langfuse (traces named issue-fix / pr-review).

features.name: Admin surface (agent runs + evaluation history)
features.description: A separate operational surface for the maintenance tooling, deliberately apart from the coach app: the frontend routes /admin/agents and /admin/evaluation and the API namespace /api/admin/*. Agent runs (issue-fix / pr-review) are listed newest-first with the selected run's investigation, plan, change, verification, PR, and review verdict shown above its full state graph - the same trace rendering as the app, inline. The evaluation view lists suite runs with each scenario's pass/fail and per-check detail, and opens any scenario's execution as a trace in an inline panel. The run history is kept in data/eval.db (`eval_runs`): one row per suite run with the kind (chat/agent), provider, model, timestamps, the pass/fail tally, and the full report as JSON - the answer to 'how has the eval been doing?' across commits.
